policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'their destruction slumbereth not' is present tense, parallel to 'lingereth not'; the same verse marks futures explicitly ('shall they ... make merchandise'), so a future nystaxei would have read 'shall not slumber'. Present nystazei.
ASV text reads 'committed them to pits of darkness' (siroi), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read chains' relegates seirais to the margin.
ASV 'condemned them with an overthrow' renders katastrophe explicitly; the omission would leave 'with an overthrow' unaccounted for.

ASV 'an example unto those that should live ungodly' fits both: the dative asebesin supports 'unto those ... ungodly', while the infinitive asebein with mellonton supports 'that should live ungodly'. The fused English phrase does not settle which construction was read, and no note is mapped here.
Presence or absence of the Greek article before dikaios leaves no trace in ASV 'for that righteous man dwelling among them'; English supplies its own determiner either way.
ASV 'bring not a railing judgment against them before the Lord' renders para kyrio (locative 'before the Lord'); the bare text has no such phrase and para kyriou would give 'from the Lord'.
ASV 'born mere animals' renders gegennemena (from gennao, 'born'); the RP gegenemena ('having become') would not yield 'born'. Word order is invisible in English but the verb form is not.
ASV 'shall in their destroying surely be destroyed' renders either the simple verb with kai or the compound kataphtharesontai; the emphatic 'surely' carries either force and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'suffering wrong as the hire of wrong-doing' renders adikoumenoi ('suffering wrong'); komioumenoi would read 'receiving' the hire.
ASV text reads 'revelling in their deceivings' (apatais), with the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read love-feasts' placing agapais in the margin.
akatapaustous and akatapastous are orthographic variants of the same sense; ASV 'that cannot cease from sin' renders either.
ASV's participle 'forsaking the right way' does not distinguish aorist katalipontes from present kataleipontes; English '-ing' carries both aspects.
ASV text reads 'Balaam the son of Beor' (Beor), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read Bosor' puts Bosor in the margin.
ASV 'and mists driven by a storm' renders kai homichlai; RP nephelai would give 'clouds'.
ASV 'the blackness of darkness hath been reserved' has no rendering of eis aiona ('for ever'), which the ASV translates where it stands.
ASV 'those who are just escaping' renders oligos ('scarcely, just'); ontos would give 'those who had indeed escaped'.
ASV 'are just escaping' is present progressive, matching the present participle apopheugontas; the aorist apophygontas would read 'had escaped'.
ASV 'of the same is he also brought into bondage' renders the kai as 'also'; the omission would leave no word for it.
ASV text reads 'the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ' without 'our', and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read our' relegates hemon to the margin.
ASV 'to turn back from the holy commandment' renders the compound hypostrepsai ('turn back'); epistrepsai would give plain 'to turn'.
ASV 'It has happened unto them' leaves a connective de untranslated as it often does at the head of a sentence; the absence of 'but' does not establish that de was absent from the text.
ASV 'the sow that had washed to wallowing in the mire' renders the verbal noun kylismon ('act of wallowing'); kylisma would name the wallowing-place rather than the act.
